newsitem.title: MEXICO: FOCUS-TV Azteca's IPO finds receptive audience.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-TV Azteca's IPO finds receptive audience.

text.p: Mexico's second-largest broadcaster, TV Azteca, on Friday launched the largest initial public offering by a Mexican company since the 1994-95 peso crisis.
Azteca, which has grown by leaps and bounds since its 1993 privatization, sold 18.5 percent of the company for a total of $526 million in a global offering in Mexico, the United States and Europe.
The issue implied an overall value for the company of $2.85 billion.

"This is to make better TV in Mexico, better programs, better newscasts," said Azteca's majority owner Ricardo Salinas Pliego during a live broadcast on his network from the floor of the Mexican bourse.
Azteca's 345,998,013 shares carried an initial offer price of $18.25 per American Depository Shares (ADS) on the New York Stock Exchange and 35.432 pesos per ordinary CPO share on the Mexican bourse.
Each CPO was made up of three shares and each ADS was worth four CPOs.
Traders scrambled to buy Azteca stock as soon as it was placed on the Mexican bourse, driving up the share price to 38.20 pesos before settling at 36.95 pesos by early afternoon.
"You know the way it goes -- there was a lot of pushing and shoving to buy it to begin with, and then they lower their bids," one trader said.
"It was the day's big news. The word is it's a good long-term buy, but not so much for day-trippers," another dealer said.
The company was only expected to take in some $50 million from the primary offer, which was nine percent of the issue.
